description: The registry distribution channel: how a signed registry reaches a peer. The Master wraps the registry in a publication, signs a digest of it with a monotonic sequence, and pushes the artifact to each peer's guard on 9090. The narrative contract is master-node/docs/registry-protocol.md; this file states the machine-checkable half so the signer, the deliverer and the peer cannot drift.

distribution.transport: the guard's existing Master-authenticated overlay route (see transport below)
distribution.why_push: The Master already dials peers on 9090 for guard approvals and the peer already has exactly one authority-plane listener that verifies the Master's key and source address. A separate pull listener would add a port and a second authentication model for a document that is already signed. Push also reaches a peer whose own entry has just been revoked, which a pull behind the peer's capability gate would not.
distribution.why_not_git: The fabric git server (4220) is spec-only and scoped to MASTER_ADMIN_PLAN.md. Distribution must not wait for that build, and a registry is a small signed document, not a repository.
distribution.delivery_note: registry-publish delivers immediately; the Master's re-delivery timer pushes the current publication every 60 s so a peer that was unreachable at publish time converges. Revocation therefore propagates to a reachable peer within one delivery interval plus the request timeout, and no later than the revoked entry's client-side checks.
distribution.offline_peer: A peer that cannot reach the Master keeps its last verified registry. That never extends authority: the entries carry expires_at, which the peer enforces locally, so a Master that stays dark cannot keep a stale grant alive past its own expiry.
distribution.bootstrap: A peer whose entry is empty or revoked still accepts a publication. The route is deliberately not gated on the peer's own capability, because revocation must be deliverable to the node it revokes.

publication.signature_travels: beside the four fields, in the same artifact; it is not part of the signed projection
publication.registry_digest: sha256 hex of json.dumps(registry, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))
publication.digest_rule: registry_sha256 must equal the digest of the registry the publication carries; a publication whose digest and document disagree is refused before any entry is read
publication.signature_covers: the projection (sequence, published_at, registry_sha256); the registry is bound by its digest
publication.sequence_rule: integer >= 1, strictly increasing across publications. A peer remembers the highest sequence it installed and refuses anything not greater, which is what makes replaying an older unrevoked registry a refusal rather than a rollback.
publication.why_digest_not_document: The registry's canonical byte form is deliberately not an authority-bearing thing: only its shape is contracted (contracts/registry-schema.json). Signing a digest binds exactly the bytes the Master published without turning a serialisation choice into a signature input.

field_semantics.sequence: monotonic publication counter. Inside the signature, so it cannot be raised (to strand a peer on a future value) or lowered (to replay) without the Master's key.
field_semantics.published_at: ISO-8601 UTC, when the Master built this publication.
field_semantics.registry_sha256: sha256 hex of the canonical registry bytes carried in this artifact.
field_semantics.registry: the registry document itself, exactly as shared/sparknet-authz.py signs and evaluates it (contracts/registry-schema.json). Not projected into the signature; bound by registry_sha256.

order: the source is loopback or the Master anchor
the publication is well formed and its digest matches its registry
the signature verifies under the peer's pinned Master key
the registry names the same Master key the peer has pinned
the sequence is strictly greater than the last installed sequence
the registry installs atomically and the installation record advances

refusals.malformed_publication: 400 - missing or extra field, bad types, or a digest that does not match the registry
refusals.bad_signature: 403 - the projection does not verify under the pinned key
refusals.wrong_master_key: 403 - the registry names a key other than the pinned one
refusals.stale_publication: 409 - the sequence is not greater than the installed one
refusals.invalid_registry: 400 - the signature is valid but the document does not satisfy contracts/registry-schema.json (shape, capability vocabulary, or an entry signature)
refusals.no_master_key: 503 - the guard has no pinned key, so it cannot verify anything
refusals.no_contract: 503 - the peer cannot load the shared contract/checker, so it cannot decide; it refuses rather than guess

acceptance.key_pinning: The peer verifies with manifests/keys/master-ed25519.pub.b64. It never trusts the key the incoming registry names; it only checks that the claim agrees with the pin.

transport.body: the five-field artifact, JSON; no wrapper and no second signature - the publication is self-authenticating
transport.source_gate: the peer accepts loopback and the Master's overlay address (10.100.0.1); every other source is refused with 403 off_overlay before the body is read
transport.idempotence: re-delivering the installed publication is refused as stale_publication (equal sequence). Re-delivery after a crash between the registry write and the record write is accepted, because the record still names the older sequence.
transport.apply_flag: installing a registry does not require --apply-enabled: that flag arms writes to protected /etc paths, and a registry lives in the peer's own vault.

implementation_state.master: built - registry-publish emits the publication, registry-deliver pushes it, the re-delivery timer converges peers
implementation_state.peer: built - the guard serves /api/v1/registry and installs atomically; sparknet-registry-client.py verifies a publication offline
implementation_state.contract_test: tests/test_contracts.py asserts this file agrees with the implementation's constants
implementation_state.live: not exercised on real hosts here; the cross-node leg is a target-node checklist item
